scope.summary: Integrate the body viewport per Section 13.27 GUI clauses: reuse the Tailor wgpu viewport with body render pipelines — skin preview shading (SSS approximation) plus heatmap overlay modes for skinning weights, UV strain, and decouple-violations — making validation state visually inspectable in the editor (13.27 validation surfaces in the viewport).
acceptance_criteria: The body renders in the shared Tailor wgpu viewport with a skin preview shading mode (approximated SSS, wet-layer preview hook) at interactive framerate on the bake-level mesh.
Overlay modes switch between: skinning weights (per selected bone), UV strain (MT-570 data), and decouple-violation heatmap (BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID findings painted on the offending vertices).
Overlay state is a typed control with a stable author_id; Argus can switch overlays and capture each mode headlessly.
capture_view (MT-604) works against this viewport including active overlays, so QA captures can show validation heatmaps.
Channel edits reflect in the viewport within one frame batch; no console errors across overlay switches.

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-633 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: Validation findings stay abstract numbers — nobody can SEE where a decouple violation or weight problem lives on the body — gutting the inspect-before-verdict loop for the highest-visual-stakes module in the product.

surfaces: BodyKit shared wgpu viewport and validation overlays

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit workspace and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Feed the shared Problems system and provide legends, units, numeric probes, stable entity links, and non-color alternatives.
BodyKit GUI must expose or integrate the geometry/morph, joint, weight/rigidity, transfer, skin/material, interlink, Jobs, Problems, history, recovery, and shared-world contracts.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
